title: The Weekend - International Workers Day

segments.en: Hello everyone, welcome back to EnglishPod.
And today we're bringing you an advanced lesson for all of our advanced learners out there.
segments.zh: 今天，我们将为您为所有高级学习者提供高级课程。

segments.en: And in this lesson, we're visiting a history class.
segments.zh: 在本课中，我们将参观历史课。

segments.en: Yes, we're going to be talking about a very interesting topic that's known around the world which is International Workers' Day.
segments.zh: 是的，我们将讨论一个非常有趣的话题，它在世界范围内广为人知，即国际工人节。

segments.en: And we're going to learn a little bit about the history of the workers' movement in the United States.
segments.zh: 我们将了解一些关于美国工人运动的历史。

segments.en: Right, but we're also going to be taking a look at some great words and of course a little bit more advanced or complicated structures.
segments.zh: 是的，但我们也将看看一些很棒的单词，当然还有一些更先进或更复杂的结构。

segments.en: So I guess without further ado, we can get started with the dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以我想事不宜迟，我们可以开始对话。

segments.en: As you know, an important aspect of becoming a good citizen is understanding the genesis of our legal system.
segments.zh: 要成为好公民，了解法律制度的起源非常重要。

segments.en: It's not enough to simply memorize our laws.
segments.zh: 仅仅记住我们的法律是不够的。

segments.en: It's necessary that we comprehend why and how they were formed.
segments.zh: 还得弄明白法律为什么、又是怎样形成的。

segments.en: This brings me to our topic for today.
segments.zh: 这让我想到了我们今天的主题。

segments.en: Does anyone know what we celebrate on May 1st?
segments.zh: 有人知道我们在 5 月 1 日庆祝什么吗？

segments.en: No, that's May 5th in Spanish, James.
segments.zh: 不，詹姆斯，那在西班牙语里是五月五日。

segments.en: No wonder you're failing my Spanish class.
segments.zh: 难怪你西班牙语课不及格。

segments.en: No, May 1st is International Workers' Day.
Do we get a day off from school then?
segments.zh: 那我们是不是可以放假一天？

segments.en: It is not considered to be a national holiday here in the US, but in other countries it is.
segments.zh: 它不被认为是美国的国定假日，但在其他国家却是。

segments.en: In the 19th century, working conditions were appalling with workers being forced to work 10, 12, and 14 hours a day.
segments.zh: 十九世纪的劳动条件十分恶劣，工人每天被迫工作十小时、十二小时，甚至十四小时。

segments.en: Support for the 8-hour workday movement was growing rapidly, despite the indifference and hostility of many union leaders.
segments.zh: 尽管许多工会领袖漠视甚至反对，支持八小时工作制的运动仍迅速壮大。

segments.en: And by April 1886, 250,000 workers were involved in the May Day movement.
segments.zh: 到 1886 年 4 月，有 250,000 名工人参与了五一运动。

segments.en: Previous legislative attempts to improve working conditions had failed, so labor organizers took drastic measures.
segments.zh: 此前改善劳动条件的立法尝试都失败了，劳工组织者于是采取了激进措施。

segments.en: They passed a resolution stating that 8 hours would constitute a legal day's work.
segments.zh: 他们通过一项决议，规定每天工作八小时才是合法工时。

segments.en: And on May 1st, 1886, the resolution took effect.
segments.zh: 1886 年 5 月 1 日，该决议生效。

segments.en: Is that why we only work 8 hours now?
segments.zh: 这就是我们现在只工作 8 小时的原因吗？

segments.en: But the happy ending came at a high price.
segments.zh: 但这样的成果付出了惨痛代价。

segments.en: On May 3rd, 1886, police fired into a crowd of strikers at the McCormick Reaper Works factory, killing four and wounding many.
segments.zh: 1886年5月3日，警方在麦考密克收割机厂向罢工人群开火，造成四人死亡、多人受伤。

segments.en: A mass meeting was called for the next day to protest the brutality.
segments.zh: 第二天召集了一次群众会议来抗议这种暴行。

segments.en: Well, as we say, the rest is history.
segments.zh: 后来的事大家都知道了。

segments.en: So we were in a history class and we learned something new, something interesting, right?
segments.zh: 所以我们在一个历史课上，我们学到了一些新的东西，一些有趣的东西，对吧？

segments.en: It's not celebrated in the US, but in many other countries it is.
segments.zh: 它不是在美国庆祝的，但在许多其他国家是这样的。

segments.en: On May 1st, a lot of people have a day off, so that's always good.
segments.zh: 5 月 1 日，很多人放假一天，所以这总是好的。

segments.zh: 你们中的许多人可能都知道创世纪是圣经中的一本书，对吧？

segments.zh: 这是圣经中的第一本书。

segments.en: And what about our last word?
After the protests ended in violence, people started to get angry because of the brutality the police showed.
segments.zh: 抗议以暴力结束后，人们开始因为警察表现出的残暴行为而生气。

segments.en: So for example, I can say, oh, I went for a run today and it was brutal.
segments.zh: 例如，我可以说，哦，我今天去跑步了，这很残酷。

segments.en: That phrase, brutal, using in that context would be for younger people maybe.

segments.en: So the teacher started with an important aspect of and then specified the idea or what part it belongs to.
segments.zh: 所以老师从一个重要的方面开始，然后指定了想法或它所属的部分。

segments.en: So it usually follows this form.

segments.en: So the teacher said that it's an important aspect of understanding the legal system was understanding its origins or its genesis.

segments.en: And then she moved on and said that it's not enough to simply memorize laws.

segments.en: It's not enough to simply do something.

segments.en: And I'm wondering about this one would.

segments.zh: 嗯，是的，我的意思是，它没有生产力，对吧？

segments.en: On May 1st, it's a holiday, and we actually have two holidays in May as well, because on the 24th, we actually celebrate the Battle of Pichincha, which is one of the decisive battles for the independence of Ecuador.
segments.zh: 5 月 1 日，这是一个假期，我们实际上也在 5 月有两个假期，因为在 24 日，我们实际上庆祝了皮钦查战役，这是厄瓜多尔独立的决定性战斗之一。

segments.en: So we don't mind having two holidays in the same month.
segments.zh: 所以我们不介意在同一个月有两个假期。

segments.en: Well, it sounds like Ecuador has a better holiday schedule than Canada.
segments.zh: 好吧，听起来厄瓜多尔的假期比加拿大的时间更好。

segments.en: So yeah, on May 1st, people take vacations, and our companies usually on May 1st will do something special for their employees.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，在 5 月 1 日，人们休假，我们的公司通常在 5 月 1 日会为他们的员工做一些特别的事情。

segments.en: Oh, that's kind of a nice gesture, isn't it?
segments.zh: 哦，这是一个很好的姿态，不是吗？

segments.en: Yeah, so it's like, it's Workers' Day, so they'll set up maybe a barbecue or a trip or something like that.
segments.zh: 是的，所以就像，今天是工人节，所以他们可能会设置烧烤或旅行或类似的东西。

segments.en: So that's what usually happens on May 1st.
segments.zh: 这就是通常在 5 月 1 日发生的情况。

segments.zh: 那么，在贵国的听众中呢？
